_comment: Published tokens/s per GPU on NVIDIA Blackwell, from SemiAnalysis InferenceX's public API
fetches every latest benchmark row for each model named in data/models.json (field 'inferencex'), keeps the
Blackwell racks and nodes, and reduces each (model, hardware, workload) to its Pareto frontier of OUTPUT tokens/s
per GPU against interactivity (median tokens/s per user) across every framework, precision and parallelism
Each point is [interactivity tok/s/user, output tok/s per GPU, input tok/s per GPU], both rates system-wide
(every GPU of the deployment counted, prefill and decode together) and taken from that run's own measured
input_tput_per_gpu / output_tput_per_gpu and prefill/decode GPU counts. Nothing is assumed about the input:output
split; the model bills input at the point's own measured input:output ratio. Rows whose input + output do not
reconstruct the row's own total within 2% are skipped (none on the seed date).
workload: '8k/1k' = 8,192 input / 1,024 output single-turn (the standard shape, used for the economics);
'1k/1k' = 1,024/1,024; 'agentx' = InferenceX AgentX agentic-coding traces (mostly cached input; shown for
reference, not used for the economics).
n = benchmark rows behind the frontier; date = newest run date among them. Benchmarks use random data with
prefix caching disabled, so they are a ceiling: the per-model realisation factor scales them.
Only a model benchmarked by InferenceX under its own name can enter the serving mix (no family or parameter
proxies). Where a model has no GB300 run but has GB200/B300/B200 runs, the GB300 rate is implied by the median
GB300:other-part ratio measured on the models that have both.
license: Apache-2.0 (per the dataset metadata on every compare page)
